hero.headline: Learn German, one clear day at a time.
hero.subline: A complete, offline German course from A1 to C2, with meanings in English, Bangla, Russian or Polish.

card.label: A word from step A1.1, as Sogda shows it, and the days it comes back after

day.title: Open the app, see today's plan, do it, done.

plan.title: Today's plan is ready
plan.body: Open Sogda and your day is laid out: what to revise, the new words, a grammar topic and a few sentences. About 10 to 20 minutes.

revise.title: Revise what's due
revise.body: The words you're about to forget come back first. Hear it, think of the meaning, then reveal.

learn.title: Learn a few new words
learn.body: Each with its article, its pronunciation, examples, and the meaning in your language. Rate how well you knew it, and Sogda picks the day it comes back.

grammar.title: The grammar topic of the week
grammar.body: A short rule and a quick practice. Get one wrong and the rule is right there.

sentences.title: Sentences from words you know
sentences.body: Practice sentences made only from words you've already learned. Tap any word for its meaning.

done.title: Day complete 🎉
done.body: That's today done. Tomorrow's plan is already waiting.

memory.title: Each word comes back just before you'd forget it.
memory.body: Sogda schedules every word with FSRS, a modern spaced-repetition method. Each time you remember a word, the wait before it comes back grows: a day, then three, then eight, then three weeks. Your minutes go to the words you're about to forget.
memory.chart: A forgetting curve: memory of a new word fades, each revision brings it back to full, and after each one it fades more slowly. The revisions come after 1 day, 3 days, 8 days and 21 days.

facts.exams: Three mock exams for every step

journey.placement: Already know some German? A short placement check starts you at the right step.
journey.road: The course as a road with {steps, number} stations, from A1.1 to C2.2, through the levels A1 Anfänger, A2 Grundstufe, B1 Mittelstufe, B2, C1 and C2.

practice.title: Quizzes, then a mock exam when you're ready.
practice.quizzes: Quizzes in every direction: German to your languages and back, articles, listening and word forms.
practice.exams: Three mock exams for every step, with vocabulary, grammar, listening, writing and speaking, and a result for each section.

features.title: Made for a real learner’s day.

offline.title: Offline, always
offline.body: No signal needed: it works on the U-Bahn and on a plane.

private.title: Private by design
private.body: No account. Your progress stays on your phone.

voice.title: Hear every word
voice.body: Your phone’s German voice, or the optional natural Supertonic voice: offline, about 400 MB, downloaded once over Wi-Fi.

compare.title: Compare near-synonyms
compare.body: Look at words like kennen and wissen side by side.

own.title: Add your own words
own.body: Keep the words you meet in daily life with the rest of your course.

widget.title: A home-screen widget
widget.body: Today’s plan at a glance, and a word of the day to hear.

reminder.title: A reminder only when it’s due

pace.title: Your pace
pace.body: A daily goal you set, with catch-up when you fall behind.

looks.title: Light, dark or glass, and easy to read.
looks.body: Pick the look you like. Text goes up to 200 %, and Sogda works with your phone’s screen reader.

languages.title: Meanings in English, Bangla, Russian or Polish.
languages.body: Pick one language, or two shown together. The pronunciation guide follows your meaning language: Bangla, Russian or Polish letters, or an English respelling. In Russian and Polish, the example sentences and grammar rules too. And the app itself comes in English, Bangla, Polish or Russian.

captions.placement: A placement check to find your step
captions.word-detail: A word in full, with examples

internet.a: No. Sogda works fully offline. Only the optional natural voice is a download, once, over Wi-Fi.

android.q: Which Android version do I need?

exams.q: Which exams does it prepare me for?
exams.a: The Goethe and telc levels from A1 to C2. Each step has three mock exams that follow their sections: vocabulary, grammar, listening, writing and speaking. They are generated from the step’s words and grammar, not official Goethe or telc papers.

sogda-vs-anki.title: Sogda or Anki for German: a ready course or your own decks
sogda-vs-anki.description: Sogda or Anki for German? Both use spaced repetition. Anki runs the decks you make or download; Sogda is a ready course, A1 to C2, offline.
sogda-vs-anki.name: Sogda or Anki
sogda-vs-anki.answer: Anki is a flashcard app: you make your own decks, or download decks other users have shared. Sogda is a ready German course from A1 to C2, with {words, number} words, {topics, number} grammar topics and {mocksPerStep, number} mock exams for every step, and both schedule your revision with spaced repetition.

body.p1: Both bring a card back just before you'd forget it. Anki's manual describes FSRS, the Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler, as an alternative to its older SM-2 algorithm that you can turn on (Anki 23.10 and later, AnkiDroid 2.17 and later). Sogda schedules every word with FSRS from the start.
Anki is the better fit when the cards are yours to make:

list.a: you want to make your own cards, for German or for anything else;
list.b: you already have a deck you trust, or want one from Anki's shared decks;
list.c: you want to set every scheduling option yourself;
list.d: you also study on a computer: Anki runs on Windows, Mac and Linux, with AnkiDroid on Android and AnkiMobile on iPhone.

body.p1: Sogda is the better fit when you want the course, not the cards:

list.a: you want the whole course ready, from your first “Hallo” to C2: {words, number} words, each with examples, its article and forms where it has them, and {topics, number} grammar topics, each with its rule and a short practice;
list.b: you want a plan for each day rather than decks to manage;
list.c: you want the meanings and a pronunciation guide in English, or in Bangla, Russian or Polish letters;
list.d: you're preparing for an exam: {mocksPerStep, number} mock exams for every step, with listening, writing and speaking, plus vocabulary and grammar;
list.e: you want it fully offline and with no account, on Android.

body.p1: Nothing stops you: take the course in Sogda, and keep an Anki deck for the words from your own work or studies that no course has.

Anki: its own manual at docs.ankiweb.net (Getting started; Deck options, on FSRS), read on 1 October 2026. Sogda: the app's course data. Anki is named here only to describe it; Sogda has no connection with it.

algorithm.a: Sogda uses FSRS, which Anki offers as an option from version 23.10; you turn it on in Anki's deck options. Anki's older SM-2 scheduler is what runs until you do.

import.q: Can I import my Anki deck into Sogda?
import.a: No. Sogda teaches its own course, so your Anki decks stay in Anki.

exam.q: Which is better for the Goethe or telc exam?
exam.a: With Anki, it depends on the deck. Sogda's steps are built around the exams, with {mocksPerStep, number} mock exams for every step that test listening, writing and speaking, plus vocabulary and grammar. They're not official papers, and there's no reading part.

iphone.a: Not yet: Sogda is on Android ({android} or newer), and iPhone is coming soon.

sogda-vs-duolingo.title: Sogda or Duolingo for German: how far, how deep, how offline
sogda-vs-duolingo.description: Sogda or Duolingo for German? Duolingo's German course goes through B2; Sogda goes A1 to C2 with grammar and mock exams, offline, no account.
sogda-vs-duolingo.name: Sogda or Duolingo
sogda-vs-duolingo.answer: Duolingo teaches many languages, and its German course goes through B2 on the CEFR scale, as Duolingo's blog said in April 2026. Sogda teaches only German, from A1 to C2 in {steps, number} steps, with {words, number} words, {topics, number} grammar topics and {mocksPerStep, number} mock exams for every step, fully offline and with no account.

body.p1: The CEFR has six levels, from A1 to C2. Duolingo's German course reaches B2, where you're an “independent user” of the language. Sogda's {steps, number} steps go on through C1 and C2, the levels of the Goethe-Zertifikat C1 and C2.
Duolingo is the better fit when German is one language among several:

list.a: you want to learn other languages in the same app;
list.b: B2 is as far as you need to go in German;
list.c: you're on iPhone today: Sogda is on Android only, for now.

body.p1: Sogda is the better fit when German is the goal:

list.a: you're aiming for C1 or C2, or for a Goethe or telc exam at any level: {mocksPerStep, number} mock exams for every step;
list.b: you want grammar as rules you can look up: {topics, number} topics, each with its rule and a short practice;
list.c: you want every word with its article and forms where it has them, examples, and a pronunciation guide in your meaning language's letters;
list.d: you learn from Bangla, Russian or Polish and want the meanings in your language;
list.e: you want it fully offline, with no account to make.

body.p1: Nothing stops you: many learners keep one app for variety and another for depth. Sogda's plan takes as long as the daily goal you set, so it fits beside another app.

Duolingo: its blog post “Duolingo Course Content Can Take You to B2 Proficiency”, 22 April 2026, read on 1 October 2026. Sogda: the app's course data. Duolingo is named here only to describe it; Sogda has no connection with it.

levels.q: How far does Duolingo's German course go?
levels.a: Through B2 on the CEFR scale, according to Duolingo's blog in April 2026. Sogda goes on to C2.

exam.q: Which is better for the Goethe or telc exam?
exam.a: Sogda's steps are built around the exams, with {mocksPerStep, number} mock exams for every step that test listening, writing and speaking, plus vocabulary and grammar. They're not official papers, and there's no reading part.

offline.a: Yes, fully, and with no account. Only the optional natural voice is a download, once, over Wi-Fi.

switch.q: Can I move my Duolingo progress to Sogda?
switch.a: No, but a short placement check starts you at the right step.
